identification: Box of three unframed prints: (1) Vanity Fair 'Men of the Day No. 1071' colour chromolithograph 'Jimmy' (golfer James Braid) by Spy (Sir Leslie Ward), published 26 June 1907, loose; (2) a Punch-style hand-coloured black-and-white cartoon 'Quick Bridge' ('One Club, One Diamond, One Heart, One Moment') on a white mount, probably 1920s-30s Punch; (3) a second Vanity Fair print of a bearded academic in cap and gown holding a birch broom, in a mount in plastic wrap, caption not legible (1870s-80s style Ape/Spy). Cannot tell from photos whether the Vanity Fair prints are originals or later reproductions.

The three items are loose prints, so check in person whether the Vanity Fair prints have the original printed title, paper age and lithographic grain (the A$9.50 eBay sales suggest cheap reprints, genuine Braid sells far higher from dealers). Read the captions and print date on the professor print; common Vanity Fair prints sell for about A$15-60 each. Terapeak AU searches for Vanity Fair returned zero (the eBay session was then blocked by a bot check), so AU sold data is thin. If the Braid print is an original, a golf print can retail A$150-300 at dealers, but I found no dated sold price at that level.
